input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, term-limited licence, failing both the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). The remaining preferred elements already sit in the contract: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology (Vendor's pre-existing IP) and applies the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence in 13.2 to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, 14.1 keeps all Customer Data rights with Customer, and 14.4 creates no joint ownership. The single edit flips ownership to Customer with Vendor's present assignment and conforms the residual sentence so our Deliverable rights are not revocable or limited to the Order Form term; Vendor's retained rights and the rest of Section 14 are untouched.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, which Vendor hereby assigns to Customer. Customer's rights to use a Deliverable are not limited to the applicable Order Form term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for: 14.2 now vests each Deliverable in Customer with a present assignment from Vendor, and the revocable, term-limited licence back to us is conformed so our Deliverable rights do not lapse with the Order Form term.
proposal.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment and remove the revocable term-limited licence

mappings.element: Customer retention of all rights in Customer Data.
mappings.quote: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights.
